question: Dime la trama de Moby-Dick; or, The Whale del autor Herman Melville.
answer:
La novela narra la historia de Ahab, capitán del ballenero Pequod, quien tras ser mutilado por un ataque de una ballena blanca llamada Moby Dick, emprende una caza obsesiva y vengativa contra el animal. El narrador, Ismael, relata desde su perspectiva los viajes de la tripulación por los mares del mundo, describiendo las complejidades de la industria ballenera y las relaciones entre los miembros del barco mientras se acercan inevitablemente al destino trágico que Ahab ha decidido enfrentar.

Este resumen se centra en el planteamiento de la obra.

Moby-Dick
sources.author: Fuente web
sources.description: == Argumento == Ishmael travels in December from Manhattan Island to New Bedford to join a whaling voyage as a green hand. At a crowded inn, he shares a bed with Queequeg, a tattooed Polynesian harpooneer and son of a king from the island of Rokovoko. The next morning, they attend Father Mapple's sermon on Jonah before heading to Nantucket. Ishmael extensively discusses cetology and introduces the crew members: chief mate Starbuck, a realist Nantucket Quaker; cheerful second mate Stubb from Cape Cod; third mate Flask; and their harpooners Queequeg, the Gay Head Indian Tashtego, and the African Daggoo. Stubb kills a sperm whale, and the cook Fleece delivers a sermon to the sharks feasting on the whale's carcass. The crew processes various harvested whale parts: liquifying congealed spermaceti, boiling blubber, decanting warm oil into casks, and stowing them in cargo.
sources.identity_text: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale is an 1851 epic novel by American writer Herman Melville. The book centers on the sailor Ishmael's narrative of the maniacal quest of Ahab, captain of the whaling ship Pequod, for vengeance against Moby Dick, the giant white sperm whale that bit off his leg on the ship's previous voyage. A contribution to the literature of the American Renaissance, Moby-Dick was published to mixed reviews, was a commercial failure, and was out of print at the time of the author's death in 1891. Its reputation as a Great American Novel was established only in the 20th century, after the 1919 centennial of its author's birth. William Faulkner said he wished he had written the book himself, and D. H. Lawrence called it "one of the strangest and most wonderful books in the world" and "the greatest book of the sea ever written". Its opening sentence, "Call me Ishmael", is among world literature's most famous. Melville began writing Moby-Dick in February 1850 and finished 18 months later, a year after he had anticipated. Melville drew on his experience as a common sailor from 1841 to 1844, including on whalers, and on wide reading in whaling literature. The white whale is modeled

literary_facts.evidence: == Argumento == Ishmael travels in December from Manhattan Island to New Bedford to join a whaling voyage as a green hand. At a crowded inn, he shares a bed with Queequeg, a tattooed Polynesian harpooneer and son of a king from the island of Rokovoko. The next morning, they attend Father Mapple's sermon on Jonah before heading to Nantucket. Ishmael extensively discusses cetology and introduces the crew members: chief mate Starbuck, a realist Nantucket Quaker; cheerful second mate Stubb from Cape Cod; third mate Flask; and their harpooners Queequeg, the Gay Head Indian Tashtego, and the African Daggoo. sources.identity_text: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale is an 1851 epic novel by American writer Herman Melville. The book centers on the sailor Ishmael's narrative of the maniacal quest of Ahab, captain of the whaling ship Pequod, for vengeance against Moby Dick, the giant white sperm whale that bit off his leg on the ship's previous voyage. A contribution to the literature of the American Renaissance, Moby-Dick was published to mixed reviews, was a commercial failure, and was out of print at the time of the author's death in 1891. Its reputation as a Great American Novel was established only in the 20th century, after the 1919 centennial of its author's birth. William Faulkner said he wished he had written the book himself, and D. H. Lawrence called it "one of the strangest and most wonderful books in the world" and "the greatest book of the sea ever written". Its opening sentence, "Call me Ishmael", is among world literature's most famous. Melville began writing Moby-Dick in February 1850 and finished 18 months later, a year after he had anticipated. question: Dime la trama de The Secret Garden del autor Frances Hodgson Burnett.
answer:
The Secret Garden narra la historia de Mary Lennox, una niña enferma y maltratada que vive en la India británica hasta que una epidemia de cólera mata a sus padres. Tras quedar sola y ser enviada a Inglaterra por su tía, Mary descubre un jardín secreto abandonado y comienza a restaurarlo junto con otros personajes, lo que le permite sanar emocionalmente y mejorar su carácter.

sources.title: The Secret Garden
The Secret Garden
sources.author: Fuente web
sources.description: == Argumento == At the turn of the 20th century, Mary Lennox is a sickly, neglected and unloved 10-year-old girl, born in British India to wealthy, self-indulgent British parents. She is cared for primarily by native servants, who spoil her and allow her to become aggressive, self-centred and unpleasant. After a cholera epidemic kills her parents, Mary is left alone when the few surviving servants flee. At first, Mary remains angry and defiant. Mary becomes interested in finding the secret garden herself, and her manners begin to soften as a result. One night, Mary follows mysterious cries that echo through the house.
sources.identity_text: The Secret Garden is a children's novel by Frances Hodgson Burnett first published in book form in 1911, after serialisation in The American Magazine (November 1910 – August 1911). Set in England, it is seen as a classic of English children's literature. The American edition was published by the Frederick A. Stokes Company with illustrations by M. L. Kirk, and the British edition by Heinemann with illustrations by Charles Robinson. Several stage and film adaptations have been made of The Secret Garden.

cards.synopsis: The Secret Garden narra la historia de Mary Lennox, una niña enferma y maltratada que vive en la India británica hasta que una epidemia de cólera mata a sus padres. Tras quedar sola y ser enviada a Inglaterra por su tía, Mary descubre un jardín secreto abandonado y comienza a restaurarlo junto con otros personajes, lo que le permite sanar emocionalmente y mejorar su carácter.

sources.title: The Secret Garden
sources.author: Fuente web
sources.description: == Argumento == At the turn of the 20th century, Mary Lennox is a sickly, neglected and unloved 10-year-old girl, born in British India to wealthy, self-indulgent British parents. She is cared for primarily by native servants, who spoil her and allow her to become aggressive, self-centred and unpleasant. After a cholera epidemic kills her parents, Mary is left alone when the few surviving servants flee. At first, Mary remains angry and defiant. Mary becomes interested in finding the secret garden herself, and her manners begin to soften as a result. One night, Mary follows mysterious cries that echo through the house.

sources.identity_text: The Secret Garden is a children's novel by Frances Hodgson Burnett first published in book form in 1911, after serialisation in The American Magazine (November 1910 – August 1911). Set in England, it is seen as a classic of English children's literature. The American edition was published by the Frederick A. Stokes Company with illustrations by M. L. Kirk, and the British edition by Heinemann with illustrations by Charles Robinson. Several stage and film adaptations have been made of The Secret Garden.
